newsitem.title: SWEDEN: More Swedes see brighter economy - poll.
newsitem.headline: More Swedes see brighter economy - poll.

text.p: The latest monthly poll from Statistics Sweden showed more Swedes believe the general economic situation will improve over the next 12 months.
The poll, carried out between April 21 and May 28 among 2,300 people, showed that the number of those who believe the economy will improve rose to 30 percent from 23 percent in the previous poll.
The poll was conducted by Swedish economic think-tank KI and the European Commission.

The number of those who believe the situation will worsen decreased to 24 percent from 28 percent, the poll showed. The number of Swedes who see the financial position of their households improving was steady at 18 percent, the poll showed.
The number of those who believe their household economies will worsen decreased to 16 percent from 17 percent.

The number of Swedes who believe unemployment will increase over the next 12 months fell to 40 percent from 45 percent. Some 19 percent of those surveyed believe unemployment would decrease compared to 15 percent a month earlier.
Consumer prices were expected to rise 1.3 percent over the next 12 months compared to 1.2 percent at the time of the last survey.
